findingReports.subject: package.json is declared as a required artifact even though no RQ/NFR in the design mandates or implies an npm/Node-based toolchain.
RQ-012 requires keyboard operator support but the design never specifies which physical keys map to ×/÷, leaving AC-012's coverage of RQ-012 unverifiable against the design.

The plan implements theme toggle logic (task 8) and creates a theme toggle control in markup (task 1), but the button-wiring task (task 5) enumerates only digit/operator/decimal/clear/backspace/equals controls and omits wiring the theme toggle control's click to the toggle logic, so no task actually connects the control to the behavior AC-016 requires.

The window-level keydown handler calls computeEquals(state) on every Enter keypress with no check of event.target, so tabbing to an on-screen button (e.g. Backspace) and pressing Enter to activate it first collapses the pending calculation via computeEquals (which sets overwrite=true) and then the button's own click-driven action (e.g. backspace(), which no-ops while overwrite is true) is silently dropped, producing an incorrect displayed result instead of the button's intended effect, e.g. entry '23' with pending operator '+' and previous 5: tabbing to Backspace and pressing Enter yields '28' instead of the expected '2'.

shouldDeferToButtonActivation suppresses the global Enter handler whenever ANY button element has focus (not just the specific button whose native activation would double-fire equals/backspace), so tabbing keyboard focus to a digit or operator button (e.g. the '5' button or '+' button) and pressing Enter appends that digit or re-selects that operator via the button's click handler instead of computing the pending calculation, reproducibly failing AC-013's requirement that Enter always trigger the same computation as the equals control.

findingDecisions.rationale: package.json had no traceability to any RQ/NFR; the design specifies a browser-only app with no installation step, so no toolchain artifact is mandated. Removed it from Declared artifacts and dropped the now-resolved open question that flagged it as a scaffolding assumption.

Revised task 5 to also wire the theme toggle control's click event to the theme toggle logic, closing the gap AC-016 requires (a control that visibly changes UI colors when toggled).

proposals.title: Clarify keyboard equivalents for × and ÷ operators (RQ-012)
proposals.problem: RQ-012 mandates keyboard input support for operators, but standard keyboards have no × or ÷ keys and the design does not state which physical keys (e.g., '*' and '/') should be treated as equivalents. This leaves the keyboard-operator acceptance criterion unverifiable against the design.
proposals.why_upstream: The missing mapping is an omission in the design's RQ-012 itself; only the design authors can decide the intended key equivalents, so the specification cannot resolve this without inventing a requirement the design never states.

# Web Calculator Specification

## Summary

A browser-based calculator supporting basic arithmetic (addition,
subtraction, multiplication, division, decimals), mouse and keyboard input,
clear/backspace editing, and a persisted light/dark theme toggle. The
application is a static, client-side web app requiring no backend, no user
accounts, and no authentication.

## Declared artifacts

index.html
src/calculator.js
src/styles.css
test/calculator.test.js

## Acceptance criteria

- AC-001: The application loads and runs entirely client-side in a modern web browser with no server-side calculation logic and no installation step.
- AC-002: The calculator UI displays number buttons for each digit 0 through 9, and selecting a digit button appends that digit to the current entry.
- AC-003: Selecting the addition (+) operator applies addition between the current entry and the next entered value when equals is pressed.
- AC-004: Selecting the subtraction (-) operator applies subtraction between the current entry and the next entered value when equals is pressed.
- AC-005: Selecting the multiplication (×) operator applies multiplication between the current entry and the next entered value when equals is pressed.
- AC-006: Selecting the division (÷) operator applies division between the current entry and the next entered value when equals is pressed, and division by zero is handled without throwing an unhandled error.
- AC-007: The calculator accepts a decimal point entry and correctly parses and computes with decimal values, allowing at most one decimal point per number.
- AC-008: A visible display area shows the current entry and, after equals is selected, shows the calculation result.
- AC-009: Selecting the clear (C) control resets the current entry, any pending operator, and the display to the initial empty state.
- AC-010: Selecting the backspace/delete control removes the most recently entered character from the current entry without clearing the entire calculation.
- AC-011: Selecting the equals (=) control computes and displays the result of the current pending calculation.
- AC-012: Pressing digit or operator keys on the keyboard produces the same entry behavior as selecting the corresponding on-screen buttons.
- AC-013: Pressing the Enter key triggers the same result computation as selecting the equals (=) control.
- AC-014: Pressing the Backspace key triggers the same character-removal behavior as selecting the on-screen backspace/delete control.
- AC-015: Pressing the Escape key triggers the same reset behavior as selecting the clear (C) control.
- AC-016: The application provides a control to switch between a Light Mode theme and a Dark Mode theme, visibly changing the UI colors when toggled.
- AC-017: The selected theme (light or dark) persists across a full page reload and across a new browser session using client-side storage.
- AC-018: The calculator layout renders correctly and remains fully usable at desktop, tablet, and mobile viewport widths, including widths as narrow as 320 pixels.
- AC-019: Each interactive button exhibits a visibly distinct hover state and a visibly distinct keyboard-focus state.
- AC-020: Text in both the light theme and the dark theme maintains sufficient color contrast against its background for readability.
- AC-021: The application loads and becomes interactive within 2 seconds on a typical broadband connection.
- AC-022: The application functions fully without requiring the user to sign in, register, or provide any authentication credentials.

## Open questions

- The design does not specify which physical keyboard keys satisfy the operator portion of RQ-012 (e.g., whether '*' and '/' are accepted as equivalents to × and ÷, or only literal '+'/'-' plus some other mapping for multiply/divide). This is left open for implementation/design clarification rather than decided in this specification.
- The design does not specify behavior for chained operator entry (e.g., entering 2 + 3 + 4 = without pressing equals between each operator). AC-003 through AC-006 are written against a simple two-operand interpretation; whether chaining should accumulate results is an open design question.

## Tasks

- Create index.html with the calculator markup: display area, digit buttons 0-9, operator buttons (+, -, ×, ÷), decimal point button, clear (C) button, backspace/delete button, equals (=) button, and a theme toggle control

- Implement operator handling in src/calculator.js for addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division, computing the result on equals and guarding division by zero so it does not throw
- Wire on-screen button clicks in src/calculator.js to the digit/operator/decimal/clear/backspace/equals state functions and the theme toggle control's click to the theme toggle logic, and update the display element to show the current entry and, after equals, the result

- Implement theme toggle logic in src/calculator.js that switches between light and dark mode by toggling a class/attribute on the document, and persists the selected theme using localStorage, restoring it on page load
- Author src/styles.css with light and dark theme color schemes, ensuring sufficient text/background contrast in both themes
- Add hover and keyboard-focus visual states for all interactive buttons in src/styles.css
- Add responsive layout rules in src/styles.css so the calculator remains usable at desktop, tablet, and mobile widths down to 320px
- Keep index.html, src/calculator.js, and src/styles.css free of any server-side logic, network calls, or authentication/sign-in requirements
- Write unit tests in test/calculator.test.js for digit entry, decimal point entry (including rejecting a second decimal), addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, division-by-zero handling, clear, backspace, and equals computation

# Product Requirements Document (PRD)

## Project Name

Web Calculator

## Purpose

Create a browser-based calculator that allows users to perform common
arithmetic calculations through an intuitive user interface. The application
shall support both light and dark themes and function entirely within a web
browser without requiring installation.

## Goals

- Provide basic calculator functionality.
- Deliver a fast and responsive user experience.
- Support both desktop and mobile browsers.
- Support user-selectable dark and light themes.
- Maintain accessibility and usability standards.

## Target Users

- General users needing quick calculations.
- Students.
- Office workers.
- Users accessing the application from desktop or mobile devices.

## Scope

### Included

- Basic arithmetic operations
- Decimal calculations
- Dark and light modes
- Responsive web interface
- Keyboard input support

### Excluded

- Scientific calculations
- Graphing functionality
- User accounts
- Calculation history synchronization across devices

## Functional Requirements

### RQ-001

The application shall run entirely within a modern web browser.

### RQ-002

The application shall provide number buttons from 0 through 9.

### RQ-003

The application shall support addition (+).

### RQ-004

The application shall support subtraction (-).

### RQ-005

The application shall support multiplication (×).

### RQ-006

The application shall support division (÷).

### RQ-007

The application shall support decimal values.

### RQ-008

The application shall display entered values and calculation results in a
visible display area.

### RQ-009

The application shall provide a clear (C) function that resets the current
calculation.

### RQ-010

The application shall provide a backspace/delete function for removing the most
recently entered character.

### RQ-011

The application shall calculate and display results when the equals (=) button
is selected.

### RQ-012

The application shall support keyboard input for numbers, operators, Enter,
Backspace, and Escape.

### RQ-013

The application shall provide both Light Mode and Dark Mode themes.

### RQ-014

The application shall persist the user's selected theme between browser
sessions.

### RQ-015

The application shall present a responsive layout that functions correctly on
desktop, tablet, and mobile screen sizes.

## Non-Functional Requirements

### NFR-001

The application shall load within 2 seconds on a typical broadband connection.

### NFR-002

The user interface shall be usable at viewport widths as small as 320 pixels.

### NFR-003

Buttons shall provide visible hover and focus states.

### NFR-004

Text shall maintain sufficient contrast in both dark and light themes.

### NFR-005

The application shall not require user authentication.
